While the story convincingly portrays the perspective of a somewhat morally ambiguous and unappealing narrator—a lonely voyeur who admits to following a strange couple home and watching them through their window—it does not provide diverse perspectives. The entire narrative is confined to the first-person viewpoint of the narrator. The other characters (the couple) are observed strictly from a distance, and their actual thoughts, motivations, and beliefs are never shared; instead, the narrator merely projects his own interpretations and unresolved grief onto their actions.
